titleEn: El Niño: when the ocean "rages" and upends the global climate
summaryEn:
El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) climate system. It occurs when sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific become unusually warm, bringing major changes in atmospheric circulation.

El Niño usually appears irregularly, about once every 2–7 years, and each event can last from several months to more than a year.
